subject: Private VPC: Next steps for VPC peering & IP allowlist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finedge.com>, Priya Malhotra <priya.malhotra@finedge.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Private VPC: Next steps for VPC peering & IP allowlist

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call:

What I heard:
- FinEdge has a strict data residency and network control requirement and is leaning toward a Private VPC deployment (customer-managed VPC peering or PrivateLink) vs hosted/dedicated.
- Your infra is on AWS (primary region us-east-1) and you want traffic to flow over private connectivity (no public internet egress for inference requests).
- Key items we need to confirm: whether you prefer VPC Peering or PrivateLink, the VPC CIDR(s) you plan to peer, and an IP allowlist for any outbound egress from your side to our peering endpoints.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please share the VPC ID(s), AWS account ID, and preferred CIDR ranges for peering.
2) Confirm whether you prefer VPC Peering (cross-account peering) or PrivateLink — we can support both; each has tradeoffs (peering is straightforward but requires non-overlapping CIDRs; PrivateLink simplifies routing but needs NLB endpoints).
3) Share any required maintenance windows for peering/routing changes and a point of contact for network engineers.
4) I attached a short network requirements template to capture the details (network-requirements-template.xlsx) — fill and return when convenient.

I'll loop in our infra lead (Sean) and security (Neha) to advise on the technical steps and requirements. Once we have the VPC/account info we'll draft a minimal peering runbook and an SOW for the work.

Thanks,

— Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: network-requirements-template.xlsx

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finedge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Malhotra <priya.malhotra@finedge.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private VPC: Next steps for VPC peering & IP allowlist

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap — that aligns with our understanding. Quick answers / clarifications:
- We're in AWS (account 987654321012) and primary VPC is vpc-0a1b2c3d in us-east-1.
- Prefer VPC Peering if possible; our infra team is more familiar with peering than PrivateLink.
- CIDR for our VPC is 10.10.0.0/16; we can open a dedicated /24 for the peering interface if you need.
- For IP allowlisting: we plan to limit egress to a set of NAT gateway Elastic IPs; I can share those once we confirm exact egress paths.
- Required ports: TLS on 443 for API traffic. We do not want public internet egress for model traffic.

Attaching our current network diagram for context (finedge-vpc-topology.pdf).

Can Sean/your team confirm any non-overlap requirement or port-level details? Also, will Redwood require cross-account IAM roles or just routing updates on our side?

Best,
Alex
Head of Infrastructure, FinEdge, Inc.
alex.johnson@finedge.com

Attachments: finedge-vpc-topology.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finedge.com>, Priya Malhotra <priya.malhotra@finedge.com>

Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private VPC: Next steps for VPC peering & IP allowlist

Alex — thanks, this is helpful. Looping in Sean (infra lead) and Vivek (solutions engineer) to confirm the technical plan. Sean / Vivek — FinEdge prefers VPC Peering, primary VPC is vpc-0a1b2c3d (10.10.0.0/16) in us-east-1. They may allocate a dedicated /24 for the peering interface and will provide NAT EIPs for allowlisting once we confirm egress.

Notes for internal review / asks for FinEdge:
- Confirm non-overlapping CIDR (they indicated 10.10.0.0/16; we must ensure Redwood's peering VPC CIDR does not overlap).
- Clarify whether they want inbound access only from our inference endpoints, or bidirectional traffic (we typically require only outbound TLS to our endpoints).
- Preferred maintenance window for route updates / testing.

Alex / Priya — we'll follow up with a short peering runbook and an SOW draft. Attached is a preliminary SOW for schedule/costing reference (sow-draft.docx). If you can confirm the account/VPC details and a preferred maintenance window this week, Sean's team can schedule the peering work next week.

Thanks — Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: sow-draft.docx

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finedge.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private VPC: Next steps for VPC peering & IP allowlist

Alex / team — thanks for the details. Quick technical checklist and timeline from our side:

High-level requirements:
- Non-overlapping CIDRs required for VPC Peering — we cannot peer if address spaces overlap. If FinEdge will allocate a dedicated /24 for the peering path that solves this.
- Ports: TCP/443 (outbound from your VPC to our inference endpoints) is the primary requirement. We do NOT require SSH (22) access into customer VPCs; if you need us to access a bastion for troubleshooting we can coordinate temporary access via a support VPN.
- Routing: Once peering is established, update route tables in FinEdge VPC to point target traffic for Redwood subnets to the peering connection. We will provide the list of Redwood subnet CIDRs to advertise.
- Security groups: Ensure outbound rules allow 443 to our endpoints. Inbound rules on our side will only allow expected IP ranges once peering is up.
- Cross-account IAM roles: Not required for basic peering; only needed if you want our operators to assume a role in your account for automation. We can proceed with manual routing changes if that is preferred.

Requested items from FinEdge to proceed:
1) AWS Account ID (you provided 987654321012 — confirm).
2) VPC ID(s) + CIDR(s) to be peered (vpc-0a1b2c3d, 10.10.0.0/16; confirm the /24 you will dedicate).
3) NAT EIP list you plan to use for any public egress (if different egress path is used).
4) Preferred maintenance window (UTC range) for peering + routing changes and a contact for the network engineer performing the work.

Timeline estimate:
- Once we have the items above, engineering can create the peering connection and validate routes in ~1 business day and schedule testing; overall target 2-3 business days to fully validate in prod, assuming no CIDR conflicts and timely coordination.

I've attached our peering-runbook (peering-runbook.pdf) that outlines the step-by-step tasks we execute.

Next: Marissa, can we lock a tentative slot for next Wed morning PST for the peering cutover, pending confirmation of FinEdge window? Alex / Priya, if that works please confirm and share the dedicated /24 and account contact.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Attachments: peering-runbook.pdf
